title: Loops, ranges, comprehensions and scope
outcome: Trace finite iteration and scope rules while using explicit empty-input and indexing policies.

exercises.title: Count an inclusive range
exercises.answer: Inclusive syntax must match the intended number of observations.

exercises.title: Use zero iterations
exercises.expected: The result is its initial zero.
exercises.hint: An empty iterable performs no loop body.
exercises.answer: The accumulator policy determines the empty-input result; other algorithms may need to reject emptiness.

exercises.title: Descend explicitly
exercises.answer: A positive default step does not produce the requested descending traversal.

exercises.title: Keep identity separate
exercises.expected: Positions are 1 and 2; values remain 10 and 20.
exercises.hint: Do not use a data value as an array index accidentally.
exercises.answer: Record identity, position and measurement are distinct roles.

exercises.title: Avoid an unnecessary collection
exercises.task: Compute only the sum of selected squares.
exercises.expected: A generator can supply the reduction directly.
exercises.hint: Ask whether the intermediate array is needed later.
exercises.answer: This changes materialization, but performance claims still need a measured workload.

exercises.title: Trace scope
exercises.task: Move a reusable accumulation into a function with explicit input.
exercises.expected: Its local state is recreated on every call.
exercises.hint: Compare the function boundary with ambient script globals.
exercises.answer: Explicit inputs and outputs make both reasoning and runtime specialization easier to inspect.
